name: Sparks
desc: An angle grinder biting steel — a jet of white-hot sparks fires from the contact point on a true ballistic arc, and the good ones deflagrate mid-flight into little carbon star-bursts before they cool to orange and die; hard, fast and industrial, nothing like a drifting ember.

energy.doc: launch speed, cone width and heat

scale.doc: throw distance + spark thickness vs design size

spray.doc: jet direction in degrees (0 = right, 90 = down, 205 = down-left)

hue.doc: spark hue (35 steel orange, 200 cold/plasma, 60 brass)

x.doc: contact point X — where the wheel meets the work

style.doc: aesthetic: white-hot steel with orange tails and carbon fork-bursts / sparse dull flint strikes, short-lived, no forks / fat slow incandescent thermite droplets / schematic ballistic traces with velocity ticks, instrument cyan

act.doc: dramaturgy: steady shower / the wheel bites in pulses driven by the musical arc / the contact point walks right across the frame

seed.doc: launch angles, speeds and which grains fork
